Subject: Acme Bank — region pinning, backups & cross-region failover (follow-up)

Hi Priya —

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for the time. Per our discovery, I wanted to capture the open items we agreed to follow up on around data residency and resiliency:

1) Region pinning: you asked whether we can guarantee that inference requests and persisted artifacts (logs, KV caches, and backups) remain in a single region (e.g., us-east-1) except during an approved failover.
2) Cross-region failover: details on how failover works, RPO/RTO expectations, and what happens to PII during failover.
3) Backups & replication: where backups are stored, frequency, and whether we support encrypted cross-region replication to a secondary region under customer control.
4) Audit/logging: what logs we retain, retention windows, and how to limit retention for PII-derived fields.
5) Next steps: technical write-up + recommendation and a short follow-up call with your infra/security team.

I've looped in Vanessa (product) to include our standard playbook and a brief answers spreadsheet — attaching our region pinning playbook and a short FAQ. We can tailor answers for your compliance needs after your security team reviews.

Next step: are you available next Tue 4/3 at 10:00am ET for a 30-min technical follow-up with your infra/security folks?

Thanks,
Aditya

Subject: Re: Acme Bank — region pinning, backups & cross-region failover (follow-up)

Thanks, Aditya — helpful recap. Quick clarifications from our side before the follow-up:

- Yes, primary requirement is that processing and persisted customer data for our EU and US customers must remain in-region unless an approved failover is triggered. We are exploring a model where US accounts are pinned to us-east-1 and EU accounts to eu-west-1.
- For failover: we need an RTO of < 15 mins for read-only traffic and < 2 hours for full read-write, if you support that model. Please call out any constraints.
- For backups: we require daily full backups and 6-hour incremental snapshots. Backups must be encrypted at rest and we prefer customer-managed keys (BYOK/KMS). Replication to a secondary region is acceptable but must be under our control or an auditable consent flow.
- Logging: we need to redact PII fields from long-term logs (beyond 30 days). Short-term operational logs (7-30 days) can contain metadata necessary for debugging but must be access-controlled.

I'll confirm availability for Tue 4/3 once I check with our security team — tentatively yes.

—Priya
Director, Cloud Security | Acme Bank
priya.singh@acmebank.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Acme Bank — region pinning, backups & cross-region failover (follow-up)

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear list. I’m Marissa’s product partner on infra-residency and will outline our standard capabilities and the recommended configuration that matches Acme's requirements. High level answers below — happy to dive deeper on the call.

1) Region pinning: Yes — Redwood supports strict region pinning at the account or tenant level. You can pin inference, model artifacts, logs, and KV caches to a single region (we commonly implement per-account routing to us-east-1 or eu-west-1).

2) Failover model & RTO/RPO: Our recommended pattern is active-passive with warm standby in the secondary region. Typical characteristics:
   - RPO: up to 6 hours for full backups (configurable down to hourly incremental snapshots)
   - RTO: read-only can be served within 10-15 minutes using replicas/promoted storage; full read-write failover typically 60-120 minutes depending on validation and DNS propagation.
   - Note: Achieving sub-15 minute full read-write RTO requires custom pre-warming and strict networking cutover (we can discuss options on the call).

3) Backups & encryption:
   - Daily full backups + 6-hour incremental snapshots are supported.
   - Backups are encrypted at rest; we support BYOK (customer-managed keys) via AWS KMS/HSM integrations.
   - Cross-region replication: supported, but we recommend you control the destination bucket/account for compliance. We can deliver an encrypted artifact to your S3 with replication configured on your side.

4) PII & logs:
   - Operational logs: default retention 30 days; can be reduced to 7 days for sensitive data.
   - Audit logs: retained per contract (we can set 1-7 years as required).
   - Redaction: We provide configurable scrubbing pipelines to remove or hash PII fields before long-term storage. You can define which fields to redact via a small mapping file.

5) Controls & evidence:
   - We can provide SOC 2 extracts, KMS key rotation logs, and a sample architecture diagram showing in-region processing.

I attached a short playbook and a template answers sheet — Marissa, can you add any implementation caveats we should surface to the security team?

Thanks,
Vanessa
Principal Product Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Acme Bank — region pinning, backups & cross-region failover (follow-up)

Hi all — adding a few implementation notes and caveats below.

1) Network egress: when we fail over, egress IPs will change to the secondary-region NAT addresses. If Acme enforces strict allowlists, we recommend adding the secondary-region egress CIDR to your allowlist ahead of time or using a Cloud VPN/Direct Connect for deterministic routing.

2) KV cache & session continuity: session KV caches are kept in-region. For cross-region failover, we replay warm caches from snapshots — there will be a short period of degraded latency while caches rebuild. We can limit session persistence windows to reduce cross-region replication scope.

3) Testing: we recommend a quarterly failover test to validate runbooks and DNS TTLs. We can help script automated failover drills to minimize human error.

Happy to walk through these on the call.

—Marissa
Senior Product Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
